title: Outside tools and code mode for mini-dsh
brief: Connect mini-dsh to tools it did not write, and let the model call tools from code. You build a small MCP client that starts a tool server as a child process, registers its tools under mcp__server__tool names on the tool registry, a skills catalogue with one skill tool, and a PTC executor whose only tool is run_code. Programs run in their own Node process and reach the harness over a private JSON-lines pipe; every call they make passes the same pre-execute, approval and post-execute checks, under a call limit and 10 parallel slots. Tests use a tiny local MCP server written in the starter and a scripted model, so nothing needs the network.

starter.note: McpClient (spawn, request with ids, line reader), publicToolName(), syncTools() with all-or-none registration.
A 40-line MCP server with one tool, get_forecast, that answers initialize, tools/list and tools/call, and can send a list-changed notice.
Reads .agents/skills/*/SKILL.md, registers the skill tool, and adds the catalogue in an agent/pre-step listener when it changes.
PtcExecutor: describe() returns only run_code; execute() refuses other names and starts the program process.
renderSdk(schemas): ToolArgsMap, ToolOutputMap, ToolCallError and tools, sorted by name, added as a prompt section.
Host side of the control pipe: invoke lines, sub-call ids, the call limit, parallel slots and tool/ptc-dispatch events.

hints: Spawn the program with a fourth pipe for control messages (stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe']), so console.log output never breaks a JSON line.
Build every MCP tool definition before you dispose the old ones; register only when the list was complete.
Test publicToolName('docs', 'search.pages') against the lesson: it must end with _23d16669848f.
Send sub-calls into the same pipeline object you use for direct calls; do not write a second, shorter path.
Count a sub-call before you validate its arguments, then check the limit: Math.floor(timeoutMs / 60000 * 1024).

rubric.criterion: The client matches each reply to its request by id and asks for the list again after a list-changed notice.
Server tools use mcp__server__tool names within 64 characters, raw names go only to the server, and registration is all or none.
The catalogue lists only names and descriptions, and the skill tool returns the full text or an error for an unknown name.
In PTC mode the model sees only run_code, a direct call to another tool fails with a clear message, and only the returned value reaches the model.
The prompt declares typed functions from the tool schemas, and calls cross a separate pipe as JSON lines with ids; an error reply becomes a ToolCallError.
Every sub-call passes the same pipeline, is logged with a parent call id, and the call limit and 10 parallel slots hold.

milestones.title: Talk to a tool server
milestones.body: Start weather-server.js, send initialize and tools/list, and call get_forecast for Paris to get 'Rain, 14 °C'.

milestones.title: Server tools in the registry
milestones.body: Register mcp__weather__get_forecast, run it through the pipeline with an ask policy for mcp__ tools, and check that a failed registration leaves no tools.

milestones.title: Skills on request
milestones.body: With three SKILL.md files, check the catalogue holds three lines, and that skill('release-notes') returns the body.

milestones.title: run_code and the channel
milestones.body: Run the line-counting program over 40 fixture files and check the result is { files: 40, total: 3120 } in two model steps.

milestones.title: Sub-call limits
milestones.body: With timeoutMs 30000, check call 513 aborts the run, 25 safe reads never exceed 10 at once, and a denied bash reaches the program as ToolCallError.
